strings.name: Andrew Feldman
strings.summary: Andrew Feldman co-founded Cerebras and leads its wafer-scale AI systems and cloud business. He previously co-founded SeaMicro, acquired by AMD in 2012. Cerebras listed on Nasdaq in 2026; chip and software achievements belong to its co-founders and engineering teams.
strings.coverageNote: Reviewed through November 17, 2026. Birth date unconfirmed. Chips and systems, trading debut and IPO closing, and criminal penalties and civil settlement are distinguished.
strings.influence.rationale: Co-founded Cerebras and advanced wafer-scale computing chips, exploring new hardware architectures for AI training and inference.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: Stanford BA in Economics and Political Science and MBA; no engineering doctorate inferred.
strings.facts.f2.label: Co-founding team
strings.facts.f2.value: Co-founded Cerebras with Gary Lauterbach, Michael James, Sean Lie and Jean-Philippe Fricker.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Wafer-scale AI computing
strings.highlights.h1.text: Company teams integrate many compute cores into wafer-scale processors with supporting systems and software; performance marketing is not independent testing of every workload.
strings.highlights.h2.title: From microservers to AI infrastructure
strings.highlights.h2.text: Participated in commercializing computing hardware at SeaMicro and Cerebras, retaining team and partner contributions to products and technology.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Comments on third-quarter results
strings.timeline.t1.text: As co-founder and CEO, discusses system sales, cloud services and customer expansion; the 2027 revenue target remains an outlook.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Cerebras begins public trading
strings.timeline.t2.text: Class A common stock starts Nasdaq trading as CBRS; the IPO closes the following day.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Company introduces WSE-3
strings.timeline.t3.text: The third-generation wafer-scale chip powers CS-3 systems; the announcement reports four trillion transistors.
strings.timeline.t4.title: WSE-2 and CS-2 debut
strings.timeline.t4.text: The company chronology dates the second-generation chip and accompanying computing system to this year.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Company unveils original WSE
strings.timeline.t5.text: Introduces an AI-oriented wafer-scale processor with more than 1.2 trillion transistors, according to the company.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Co-founds Cerebras
strings.timeline.t6.text: Five co-founders launch the wafer-scale computing venture; filings date his CEO and president tenure from April 2016.
strings.timeline.t7.title: AMD completes SeaMicro acquisition
strings.timeline.t7.text: The microserver company he co-founded and led as CEO joins AMD’s data-center server business.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Historical accounting-controls sentence
strings.timeline.t8.text: After pleading guilty in the Riverstone-related case, receives three years’ probation and a $5,000 fine; a separate 2008 SEC civil settlement neither admits nor denies the allegations.
